english.notes:
(i) See Section 43(1)(a) and (b) of the Solicitors Act 1974, which sets out the conditions under which the defendant may have an order under Section 43(2) of the Act made against him.
(ii) Section 44(3) states that any document purporting to be an order under Section 43(2) and to be duly signed in accordance with Section 48(1) of the Act shall be received in evidence in any proceedings and deemed to be such an order without further proof unless the contrary is shown.
(iii) Proceedings under this section may be commenced at any time before the expiration of six months after the first discovery of the offence by the prosecutor, but no proceedings may be commenced, without the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, but any person other than the Society or a person acting on behalf of the Society.
